messages:
alex: FYI — jess filed an escalation: iOS app is dropping SSE streams mid-response when the phone switches networks (WiFi -> cellular) or when the app backgrounds. Happening consistently on app v2.7.1. Attaching the user's repro notes below.

jess (Customer): Repro steps I did: open chat, start a long streaming reply (10+ tokens/sec), then toggle WiFi off (so it forces cellular) after ~12s. The stream stops and the UI shows 'connection lost' but partial content stays. Happens ~4/5 tries. iOS 16.5, iPhone 12. App v2.7.1.

devin (Mobile): Thanks for the repro, jess. Quick q: are you using native URLSession SSE polyfill or a third-party EventSource? Also are you seeing any token refresh right at the same time? iOS will often tear sockets on interface change or backgrounding — depending on the run loop and background modes.

alex: They said it's our default EventSource polyfill in the SDK. No explicit token refresh at that moment. No error body returned from server — just the stream stops.

mia (Backend): I pulled backend logs for jess's user_id for the timeframe and see a bunch of 499/connection closed records where the server was mid-chunk. Sample:

```
2026-02-21T18:32:45Z stream_id=st_7a9c user=jess event=chunk_sent bytes=2048
2026-02-21T18:32:46Z stream_id=st_7a9c user=jess event=write_error err="write: connection reset by peer"
2026-02-21T18:32:46Z stream_id=st_7a9c user=jess event=status=499
```

mia: This suggests the TCP connection closed from the client side (or intermediate proxy). Not seeing an application-level error.

jonah (SRE): If it's happening on WiFi -> cellular, two common culprits: 1) mobile OS tears the socket on interface change, 2) load balancer or proxy idle/keepalive policies drop connections during the handover. ALBs have an idle timeout (defaults 60s) and some mobile networks aggressively reset connections. Can we confirm whether the request traverses an ALB / nginx? Also we should check for `TCP FIN` vs `RST` in the logs.

alex: Our path uses an ALB in front of the runtime. mia, can you grep for `connection: close` or TCP reset markers around those times?

mia (Backend): Grepped. Most entries show `write_error: connection reset by peer` (RST). Example from upstream proxy logs: `client=10.2.3.4:54782, server=10.10.10.12:8080, request="GET /v1/streams...", upstream_status="499"`. No server-side Close.

devin (Mobile): iOS specifics: when switching networks, sockets often get an RST. EventSource doesn't automatically reconnect if the app is backgrounded and the OS stops network tasks. Two mitigation ideas: 1) short-term: implement client reconnection logic on `onerror` that retries and resumes using `last-event-id` or by requesting continuation token. 2) server-side keepalive pings (send a `:
` comment or 1-byte keepalive every ~15s) to prevent intermediate proxies from thinking the stream is idle.

alex: Can you reproduce locally with a phone? jess reported toggling WiFi quickly triggered it. I want a minimal curl repro too.

jess (Customer): I can repro — I'll try with my phone and send a packet capture if needed.

mia (Backend): I tried reproducing with `curl -N` and toggling network on a Mac; I see the same pattern: server keeps writing but the client side reports `Connection reset by peer`. Curl output:

```
$ curl -N -H "Accept: text/event-stream" "https://api.redwood.example/v1/streams/abcd"
:data: token chunk 1
:data: token chunk 2
[then toggle wifi]
curl: (18) transfer closed with outstanding read data remaining
```

mia: Server-side quick fix candidate: emit a SSE comment keepalive (`:
`) every 15s while stream active to keep LB/proxies from idling it out. That won't help if iOS itself RSTs during interface change, but it will help intermittent proxy timeouts.

jonah (SRE): Agree. Also recommend we bump ALB idle timeout to 120s for the canary and enable TCP keepalive with shorter probe intervals on the runtime instances. If we still see lots of RSTs keyed to mobile carriers, that's client-side or carrier-level and we'll need to rely on reconnect and resume semantics.

devin (Mobile): On the SDK side I can add a reconnect strategy that: detect `onerror`, attempt exponential backoff reconnects, preserve partial stream by requesting a resume token from the server (we already issue a `stream_resume_id` in metadata). Also will try toggling HTTP/2 -> HTTP/1.1 fallback — sometimes ALBs treat those differently.

mia (Backend): Quick prototype server patch I pushed to infra branch: send keepalive every 15s and add `X-Stream-Resume: <id>` header in the initial response so clients can ask for resume. Config snippet:

```
streaming.keepalive.interval=15s
streaming.resume_header= X-Stream-Resume
```

mia: I'll open a canary deploy on staging with keepalive enabled.

jonah (SRE): I'll schedule ALB idle timeout change on the canary and enable instance-level TCP keepalive (probe interval 30s, retries 3) on the runtime group. I'll monitor `stream_disconnect_rate` and `rst_counts` per carrier.

alex: Next actions: (1) mia deploy keepalive canary on staging, (2) jonah change ALB idle on canary, (3) devin add SDK reconnect/resume in next patch and ship a test build to jess, (4) jess to run repro and optionally share pcap if problem persists.

jess (Customer): Thanks — I'll test the test build once available. Happy to share pcap if you need packet-level debugging.

alex: Great — ping me when the staging canary is live and we'll coordinate with jess for verification. Thanks all. :thumbsup:
